title: Refit a plug-in coil burner after cleaning: bowl opening to the hidden receptacle, terminals pushed in, coil let down
keywords: blind sideways insertion under a lip
instruction: Put the coil burner back in its burner well so that it is plugged in and lies flat in its drip bowl, then let go.
context: Anyone who cooks on an electric coil range lifts the plug-in burners out to wash the chrome drip bowls under them, then puts them back. GE's owner's manuals give the way: "Replace the drip pan into the recess in the cooktop. Make sure opening in the pan lines up with the receptacle." "Insert the terminals of the surface unit through the opening in the drip pan and into the receptacle." "Guide the surface unit into place so it rests evenly." The receptacle is hidden under the cooktop's edge, so the terminals can only go in sideways, through the bowl's opening: the coil is held tipped up at the far side, pushed in blind until its terminals are home past their spring contacts, then let down about the terminals until it lies flat. Set straight down, it lands on its terminals on the cooktop's edge, unplugged; with the bowl's opening turned away, the leads hit the bowl. The skill is a blind sideways plug-in under a lip followed by a pivot down, not a placement from above.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. (1) Cooktop section, fixed, true size: white enamelled steel top 3 mm thick, its top 7.5 cm up, x 6 to 40, y -25 to 33, on a housing down to the table, with a round burner well (hole 22.6 cm across) centred at x 20.5, y -5.0. (2) Plug-in receptacle, fixed, hidden under the top's edge on the robot's right of the well: its face 12.2 cm from the well's centre (y -17.2); two slots 6.5 mm wide, 10 mm tall, 3.2 cm deep, 22 mm apart, their mouths flared 3 mm, each with a spring contact a terminal pushes about 0.9 mm aside; the terminals' line 1.3 cm below the top. (3) 8-inch chrome drip bowl (like GE WB32X10014), loose, 0.20 kg: flange 24.8 cm across resting on the top round the hole, 4.0 cm deep, sides sloping from 22.2 to 17.0 cm across, a 5 cm centre hole; the opening in its side, 4.3 cm wide and 2.6 cm deep, points to the back (+x), a quarter turn from the receptacle. (4) 8-inch plug-in coil element (like GE WB30M2), loose, 0.55 kg: 5 turns of 8 mm tube 20.8 cm across with a 52 mm opening in the middle, on a three-legged support 4.3 cm tall; two terminals 4.8 mm across, 22 mm apart, 29 mm long on a bracket, 25.2 cm from the far side to their tips. It lies on its legs on the top centred at x 20.5, y 23.5, its terminals pointing toward the well (-y). Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run. 0: the bowl's opening more than 15 deg from the receptacle's direction, or the bowl not resting flat in its recess (tilt 2 deg or more, flange 2 mm or more off the top, or off centre 6 mm or more). 0.25: the bowl right, the coil not plugged in. 0.5: the bowl right and both terminals in the receptacle (each tip 20 mm or more past the receptacle's face, and each spring contact pushed aside 0.4 mm or more by its terminal), but the coil not flat on its legs, still held, or not still. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): the bowl right, plugged in, the coil flat (tilt under 2 deg) and resting on its legs in the bowl (centre within 2 mm of its seated height), every finger point 2 cm or more from the coil, and the coil still (under 1 mm in 1 s). Nothing is latched. Real trial: the bowl's opening against a mark at the receptacle; plugged in checked with a torch under the edge and by the coil's centre within 6 mm of the well's centre (tape from the bowl's rim on both sides); flat with a small spirit level both ways; let go and still on the video.
reset_notes: Lift the coil's far side about 1.5 cm, pull the coil straight out of the receptacle and lay it on its legs on the top at its mark, terminals toward the well; turn the bowl so its opening points to the back. Nothing is consumed. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. Sizes from GE listings (coil 7 7/8 in, 9.75 to 10 in with terminals; bowl 9.75 in, 1.75 in deep). Receptacle slot and contact sizes, masses and frictions (coil 0.8, receptacle 0.2) are estimates. The spiral is five rings of capsules, the bowl 48 flat segments; each spring contact is a hinged leaf on a 0.4 N m/rad spring. The range is off and cold: no wiring or heat. Real rig: a steel or plywood top with a real receptacle.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left gripper went down onto the coil on the cooktop and pushed at it but never lifted it; the right gripper stayed by the cooktop's right edge; the bowl was never turned); demo: 1.0
